header.stance: 美國固定收益市場因六月節休市；全球政策與通膨風險有待6月22日開市後消化

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 假期固定收益市場簡報

依SIFMA建議，美國固定收益市場6月19日因六月節全面休市，當日沒有美國公債價格發現。下一個正常交易日為6月22日，屆時投資人將開始消化假日期間累積的消息，包括英國財政不確定性再起、歐洲物價數據轉強，以及日本貨幣政策辯論進一步升溫。

其他歐洲市場照常交易之際，Andy Burnham以壓倒性優勢贏得國會席次，取得挑戰首相Keir Starmer的機會，英國公債隨之走弱。10年期英國公債殖利率上升5個基點至4.81%；在石油引發的通膨壓力持續之際，選舉結果又推升財政風險溢價。Burnham在投票前幾乎未具體說明舉債政策，投資人關注領導層一旦更替，是否可能放寬原本有助維持市場對英國債務信心的財政框架。

這項不確定性在週末進一步升高。儘管Burnham已公開承諾維持現行規則，其顧問團隊中的經濟學家與政策人士仍主張拉長財政評估期間，為公共投資保留更多空間。截至本次資訊期間結束，Starmer已提出離任時程，潛在競爭者也支持迅速完成交接。這降低了領導權之爭久拖不決的可能性，卻也讓財政政策問題更快成為焦點。

日本則釋出已開發市場最明確的新緊縮信號。日本央行副總裁冰見野良三警告，企業加快轉嫁成本，可能波及各類消費品與服務，推動基礎通膨升破2%目標。日本央行先前已將政策利率調升至1%；冰見野並將進一步緊縮定位為預防措施，以免日後被迫採取更急劇的行動。

休市期間，地緣政治情勢也有變化。原訂週五舉行的美國與伊朗談判因黎巴嫩爆發戰事而延後；其後儘管出現新的威脅，伊朗方面對談判是否中止的說法也相互矛盾，雙方仍於週末在瑞士展開會談。華府並核發60天許可，允許伊朗在談判持續期間出售石油。這為供給增加提供了可能，但雙方對核計畫查核仍有歧見，荷莫茲海峽的安全也未明朗，因此對通膨的影響仍取決於後續發展，尚無定論。

## 全球利率、信用與主權債市動態

Burnham在Makerfield補選中取得24,927票，英國改革黨候選人則不到16,000票。勝選幅度強化了他接替Starmer的訴求，但債市擔心的重點並非領導權之爭本身，而是Burnham周邊逐漸成形的政策聯盟。

Burnham承諾保留現行規則，包括經常性支出須由稅收支應，以及債務占經濟比重必須下降。不過，他身邊多名顧問認為這些限制過於短視。英國央行前首席經濟學家Andy Haldane與高盛前首席經濟學家Jim O’Neill均主張提高舉債能力以支應投資；英國預算責任辦公室前主席Richard Hughes則批評，現行框架在遭遇衝擊後，修正舉債的速度過慢。

Burnham盟友Louise Haigh提出的其中一項方案，是把債務規則的評估期間，從目前3年及5年的滾動區間延長至約10年。這可在不正式放棄財政紀律的情況下，創造更多近期投資空間，但也意味投資人必須接受更漫長的債務回穩路徑。英國財政研究所支持重新檢視現行規則所形成的誘因，但警告任何調整都只能在財政公信力穩固的前提下進行。

眼前的考驗可能落在Thames Water。政府本週否決了債權人提出的紓困方案，而Burnham陣營中的一些人士支持加強公共部門對必要服務的控制。若實施國有化，這家公用事業公司的龐大債務是否會轉移至政府資產負債表，將成為市場關注的問題。

英國經濟活動數據也讓英國公債前景更為複雜。5月零售銷售量月增1.2%、年增3.2%，4月降幅則由1.3%修正為1.0%。最近3個月銷售量增加0.4%，非店面銷售月增6.1%，創2025年2月以來最大單月增幅。這波反彈顯示，即使財政與能源風險持續推高借款成本，家庭需求仍具韌性。

英國央行另為私人市場的全系統壓力測試設定嚴苛參數。參與測試的46家公司包括Apollo、Ares、Blackstone、KKR、Pemberton、BlackRock、Legal & General Investment Management及Fidelity International，以及為私人資產提供融資的銀行與機構投資人。

測試情境假設全球經濟陷入長達5年的嚴重衰退。初期情境包括通膨升至7%、資產價格普遍下跌，以及波動率指數升至40。第2年則同時假設英國GDP萎縮4%、英國股市下跌35%、利率升至7%，槓桿貸款利差擴大400個基點。後續幾年僅緩慢復甦，失業率為7.5%，GDP成長率為0.7%。

由於私人信貸與私募股權已成為人工智慧產業的重要資金來源，AI融資是這次測試的核心。情境假設能源價格上漲與硬體短缺推高成本、延緩模型開發，並限制近期生產力增益。參與機構將先說明因應方式，收到市場整體反應後再修訂計畫。首批資料須於7月提交，最終報告預定2027年發布。

歐元區決策官員持續強調通膨的持續性。歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane為6月將存款利率調升至2.25%的決定辯護，認為通膨高於目標，經濟與金融情勢又保持韌性，因此按兵不動難以合理化。由於已形成的成本上漲仍將陸續反映至物價，他預期2026年剩餘期間通膨率都會維持在3%以上。

Lane也重申，估計中性利率區間的上緣已升至約2.5%。依此判斷，歐洲央行仍有再升息25個基點的空間，而不必然使政策明顯轉為限制性；但最終利率路徑仍取決於能源及其他企業成本是否繼續轉嫁至消費價格。

德國生產者物價進一步強化這項疑慮。5月工業產品價格月增0.3%、年增2.2%，年增幅高於4月的1.7%。排除能源後，價格月增0.7%、年增2.3%；中間財價格年增4.2%，顯示壓力並不限於能源。能源價格雖年增2.5%，但5月單月下跌0.4%。

捷克央行4年來首次升息後，當地另爆發一場央行政策爭議。總理Andrej Babis批評這項決定，主張國內貨幣政策無法實質影響通膨，只會傷害借款人。央行總裁Ales Michl則捍衛央行獨立性，並以放款成長加快、政府舉債、工資快速成長及服務通膨持續為緊縮理由。

日本的政策討論已從6月升息，轉向支持日本央行緊縮的多數能否維持。冰見野表示，較高投入成本正在企業交易鏈中加快傳導，可能帶動各類消費價格上漲。日本5月企業投入價格年增6.3%，為3年來最快。冰見野也表示，若供給面帶動的漲價充分擴散並推高基礎通膨，貨幣政策可能需要作出回應。

日本央行總裁植田和男已出院；他先前缺席6月會議，預定於6月23日復職。植田在履行公務期間，仍將持續接受約兩週的門診治療。

6月決策中唯一的反對票凸顯了較長期的限制。新任審議委員淺田統一郎反對將利率調升至1%，本月另有一名被視為支持寬鬆政策的新任委員即將加入。兩名立場鮮明的鷹派委員約一年後任期屆滿，政府屆時將再有機會重塑這個9人決策委員會。會後受訪的經濟學家略多於半數預期下次升息在12月，36%選擇10月；政策利率峰值的預估中位數則由1.5%升至1.75%。

日本主權債標售顯示，短端及非最新券均有需求。3個月期國庫貼現券標售的加權平均殖利率為0.9107%，低於6月12日標售的0.9294%；最低得標價格所對應的殖利率為0.9224%，前次為0.9387%。競爭性投標總額為¥9.638兆，其中¥3.150兆獲得接受，債券於9月24日到期。

另一場流動性供給標售涵蓋剩餘期限5至11年的JGB，投標總額¥1.898兆，接受金額為¥6,489億。平均得標利差較參考利率高0.016個百分點，最高得標利差高0.020個百分點。日本這兩項操作均於6月22日交割。

印度債市面臨的是另一種流動性問題。6月5日減稅措施鼓勵外資投資債券後，5年期政府債殖利率已下跌逾30個基點至6.49%。美國銀行與Bandhan AMC分析師警告，若印度央行收回銀行體系的過剩資金，短端漲勢可能失去動能。

近期繳稅後，銀行體系剩餘流動性僅約2,940億盧比；隨著政府支出及印度央行股利移轉把資金送回銀行，規模可能升向8兆盧比。附賣回操作可能吸收其中一部分，DBS則預期銀行現金準備要求可能在8月調高。印度央行的美元遠期部位到期，也會收回盧比流動性。

與此同時，至少4家印度放款機構正利用印度央行一項年利率1.5%的換匯機制，籌備合計約$25億的美元債發行。印度國家銀行可能籌集最多$10億，Axis Bank、Bank of Baroda及Power Finance Corp.則各自考慮發行至少$5億，期限主要為5年。在國內信貸成長持續超過存款成長之際，這項機制可降低美元融資成本；但由此產生的外資流入，也可能增加印度央行日後需要回收的流動性。

加拿大4月零售報告的內部結構弱於表面數字。名目銷售額增加0.5%至C$730億，略低於0.6%的預期，也慢於3月的0.9%增幅。銷售量持平，排除燃料與汽車的核心指標則下降0.7%。燃料供應商收入增加5.1%，汽車銷售成長1.7%。加拿大統計局根據涵蓋52.1%受訪企業的回覆，初步估計5月零售銷售將成長1.0%。

俄羅斯央行也調降關鍵利率，但降幅小於經濟學家預期。貨幣升值及石油收入增加協助5月通膨降至5.3%，不過官員仍須面對財政擴張、燃料價格壓力，以及中東衝突推升的物流成本傳導至國內物價等風險。在國營相關部門以外的投資轉弱之際，低於預期的降息幅度維持了央行的審慎立場。

企業信用方面，SpaceX推進投資等級債券發行，預計至少籌集$200億。這筆交易是規模更龐大的募資計畫之一，資金將用於人工智慧基礎設施及太空資料中心。自11月以來，Alphabet、Amazon及其他AI相關借款人已在各類信用市場籌集逾$3,000億。AI這項資本密集題材已主導發行市場，SpaceX交易將考驗投資人還願意承接多少額外曝險。

聯準會治理也受到關注。負責監管事務的副主席Michelle Bowman於6月17日出席美國銀行私人晚宴，當時距FOMC會議結束僅數小時，且仍在央行對外溝通緘默期內。Bowman表示，她並未討論貨幣政策，且遵守了所有FOMC及道德規範。此事發生之際，主席Kevin Warsh正著手檢討聯準會與投資人及公眾溝通的方式。

## 下一個交易時段觀察重點

6月22日美國市場重開時，多項發展將同時納入美國利率定價，包括恢復舉行的美國與伊朗談判、60天石油銷售許可、英國領導層更替，以及假日期間累積的全球通膨數據。地緣政治的主要不確定性，在於談判能否恢復荷莫茲海峽安全且持續的通行。雙方對核計畫查核說法不一，加上區域戰事持續，結果仍未明朗。

中國將於6月22日上海時間09:00公布6月貸款市場報價利率。1年期利率現為3.00%，5年期為3.50%，市場預期兩者均維持不變。本次報價結果將顯示，近期流動性措施能否在未再次正式降息的情況下，傳導至放款基準利率。

加拿大同日將於美東時間08:30公布5月消費者物價。整體通膨率預計由2.8%升至3.0%；這是消費籃子更新後首次公布的數據，對能源成本轉嫁的檢驗，將比4月名目零售銷售增幅更直接。

美國公債在假期後的首批供給，是6月22日標售$890億13週期國庫券及$770億26週期國庫券，兩者均於6月25日交割；6月23日另有$650億6週期國庫券。附息債供給由6月23日$690億新發行2年期公債揭開序幕，6月24日接續標售$700億新發行5年期公債，6月25日再標售$440億新發行7年期公債，三者均於6月30日交割。在聯準會6月訊息更聚焦通膨後，這一連串供給將檢驗政策敏感型及中期債券的需求。

日本主權債需求的下一項考驗，是6月23日規模約¥2.5兆的5年期JGB標售。6月25日還將增額發行約¥7,000億、2046年3月到期的20年期JGB。日本央行持續緊縮且決策委員會組成逐步變化之際，標售結果有助區分中期債券需求，以及影響較長天期債券的期限溢價壓力。

美國主要總經數據將集中於6月25日美東時間08:30公布。市場預期5月個人所得月增0.4%、支出月增0.6%、整體PCE物價月增0.5%，核心PCE物價月增0.3%；PCE年通膨率則預計由4月的3.8%加速至4.1%。耐久財訂單在前月增加7.9%後，預計下跌5.0%；第1季GDP第3次估值的年化成長率預計為1.7%，高於前次估值的1.6%。初領失業救濟人數前值為22.6萬，這項數據將顯示近期續領人數增加，是否正演變成更廣泛的勞動市場疲弱。

墨西哥央行將於6月25日晚些時候公布決策。目前隔夜目標利率為6.50%，市場預期維持不變。能源通膨及美元進一步升值的風險，將決定決策官員是否繼續把寬鬆循環視為已經結束。

overall_summary.headline: 美國債市休市之際，英國財政風險與全球通膨壓力升高
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國固定收益市場因六月節全面休市，當日沒有美國公債價格發現。歐洲市場照常交易，Andy Burnham以壓倒性優勢贏得國會席次，取得接替首相Keir Starmer的途徑，帶動10年期英國公債殖利率上升5個基點至4.81%。即使Burnham已承諾維持現行規則，市場仍擔心主張拉長財政評估期間、增加舉債以支應投資的顧問，可能削弱原本支撐英國債務信心的框架。

歐洲通膨信號也轉強。歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane為存款利率調升至2.25%的決定辯護，並預期2026年剩餘期間通膨率都將高於3%；德國5月生產者物價年增率則加速至2.2%。日本方面，日本央行副總裁冰見野良三警告，企業成本更快轉嫁可能推動基礎通膨升破2%目標。在政策利率已升至1%後，這進一步強化了繼續緊縮的理由。

美國與伊朗談判先前延後，其後於瑞士恢復，華府並核發60天許可，允許伊朗在談判期間出售石油。此舉為供給增加提供了可能，但雙方對核查仍有歧見，區域戰事持續，加上荷莫茲海峽能否安全通行尚不確定，使6月22日美國市場重開前的通膨影響仍無定論。

section_summaries.summary: 美國固定收益市場因六月節全面休市，沒有美國公債價格發現；6月22日開市時，市場須消化Andy Burnham勝選後10年期英國公債殖利率上升5個基點至4.81%、轉強的歐洲物價信號、更偏鷹派的日本央行政策辯論，以及美國與伊朗恢復談判所牽動、仍取決於後續發展的石油風險。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

U.S. fixed-income markets were fully closed on June 19 for Juneteenth under SIFMA’s recommendation, leaving no same-day Treasury price discovery. The next regular U.S. session is June 22, when investors will begin absorbing a holiday window marked by renewed UK fiscal uncertainty, firmer European price data and a further sharpening of Japan’s policy debate.

Gilts weakened while other European markets were open after Andy Burnham’s decisive parliamentary victory gave him a route to challenge Prime Minister Keir Starmer. The 10-year gilt yield rose 5 basis points to 4.81%, with the election result adding a fiscal-risk premium as oil-related inflation pressure persisted. Burnham had offered little detail on borrowing policy before the vote, and investors focused on whether a change of leadership could loosen the fiscal framework that has helped preserve confidence in UK debt.

That uncertainty increased over the weekend. Burnham’s advisers include economists and policy figures who have argued for longer fiscal horizons and more room for public investment, even though he has committed publicly to the existing rules. By the end of the information window, Starmer had set out a timetable for his departure and potential rivals were backing a rapid transition, reducing the prospect of a prolonged leadership contest but bringing the fiscal-policy question closer.

Japan supplied the clearest new developed-market tightening signal. Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino warned that faster business-cost pass-through could spread across consumer goods and services and push underlying inflation above the 2% target. His remarks followed the BOJ’s increase in its policy rate to 1% and framed further tightening as protection against having to move more abruptly later.

The geopolitical backdrop also changed during the closure. US-Iran negotiations scheduled for Friday were postponed after fighting in Lebanon, then began in Switzerland over the weekend despite new threats and conflicting Iranian reports about whether the talks had stopped. Washington issued a 60-day license permitting Iranian oil sales while negotiations continued. The move offered a path toward greater supply, but disagreement over nuclear inspections and the security of the Strait of Hormuz left the inflation implications conditional rather than settled.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

Burnham won 24,927 votes in the Makerfield by-election, compared with fewer than 16,000 for Reform UK’s candidate. The scale of the victory strengthened his claim to replace Starmer, but the bond-market concern was less the leadership contest itself than the policy coalition forming around Burnham.

He has pledged to retain rules requiring current spending to be covered by tax receipts and debt to decline as a share of the economy. Several advisers around him, however, have called those constraints too short-termist. Former BOE Chief Economist Andy Haldane and former Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Jim O’Neill have argued for greater borrowing capacity to fund investment, while former Office for Budget Responsibility chair Richard Hughes has criticized the slow correction of borrowing after shocks under the present framework.

One proposal from Burnham ally Louise Haigh would extend the horizon for assessing the debt rule to about 10 years from the current three- and five-year rolling windows. That could create more near-term investment room without formally abandoning fiscal discipline, but it would also require investors to accept a longer path toward stabilization. The Institute for Fiscal Studies has supported reconsidering the incentives created by the rules while warning that changes should come only from a position of credibility.

The immediate test could involve Thames Water. The government rejected a creditor rescue plan during the week, and figures in Burnham’s circle have supported greater public control of essential services. Nationalization could raise questions over whether the utility’s substantial debt would migrate to the public balance sheet.

UK activity data added another complication for the gilt outlook. Retail-sales volumes increased 1.2% in May and 3.2% from a year earlier, while April’s decline was revised to 1.0% from 1.3%. Volumes were 0.4% higher over the latest three months, and non-store sales jumped 6.1%, their strongest monthly increase since February 2025. The rebound indicated that household demand remained resilient even as fiscal and energy risks kept pressure on borrowing costs.

The BOE separately set demanding parameters for a system-wide stress test of private markets. The exercise will involve 46 firms, including Apollo, Ares, Blackstone, KKR, Pemberton, BlackRock, Legal & General Investment Management and Fidelity International, as well as banks and institutional investors that finance private assets.

The scenario assumes a severe five-year global downturn. Its early stages feature inflation at 7%, a broad asset-price fall and a volatility index at 40. The second year combines a 4% decline in UK GDP, a 35% fall in UK shares, interest rates at 7% and a 400-basis-point widening in leveraged-loan spreads. Later years assume only a slow recovery, with unemployment at 7.5% and GDP growth of 0.7%.

Artificial-intelligence financing is central to the exercise because private credit and private equity have become important sources of capital for the sector. The scenario assumes higher energy prices and hardware shortages raise costs, slow model development and limit near-term productivity gains. Participants will first describe how they would respond, then revise those plans after receiving an aggregate view of the market’s reaction. Initial information is due in July, with a final report scheduled for 2027.

Euro-area policymakers continued to emphasize inflation persistence. European Central Bank Chief Economist Philip Lane defended the June increase in the deposit rate to 2.25%, arguing that above-target inflation and resilient economic and financial conditions made an unchanged decision difficult to justify. He expects inflation to remain above 3% for the rest of 2026 because of cost increases already in the pipeline.

Lane also reiterated that the upper end of the estimated neutral-rate range has risen to about 2.5%. That assessment leaves room for another quarter-point increase without necessarily making policy materially restrictive, although the eventual path still depends on whether energy and other business costs continue reaching consumer prices.

German producer prices strengthened that concern. Industrial prices rose 0.3% in May and 2.2% from a year earlier, accelerating from 1.7% in April. Excluding energy, prices increased 0.7% on the month and 2.3% over 12 months. Intermediate-goods prices were 4.2% higher than a year earlier, showing that the pressure was broader than energy, which rose 2.5% annually but declined 0.4% during May.

A separate central-bank dispute emerged in the Czech Republic after the Czech National Bank raised rates for the first time in four years. Prime Minister Andrej Babis criticized the move, arguing that domestic monetary policy could not meaningfully influence inflation and would instead hurt borrowers. Governor Ales Michl defended the bank’s independence and cited stronger lending, state borrowing, rapid wage growth and persistent services inflation as reasons for tightening.

Japan’s policy discussion moved beyond the June increase toward the durability of the BOJ’s tightening majority. Himino said higher input costs were passing through business transactions faster and could lift a broad range of consumer prices. Japanese corporate input prices had risen 6.3% from a year earlier in May, the fastest pace in three years. He also said supply-driven increases could warrant a policy response if they spread sufficiently to raise underlying inflation.

Governor Kazuo Ueda was discharged from hospital and is scheduled to return on June 23 after missing the June meeting. He will continue outpatient treatment for about two weeks while performing his official duties.

The June decision’s single dissent highlighted a longer-term constraint. New board member Toichiro Asada opposed the increase to 1%, and another appointee associated with accommodative policy is due to join the board this month. Two prominent hawks will complete their terms in about a year, giving the government further opportunities to reshape the nine-member board. Just over half of economists surveyed after the meeting expected the next increase in December, while 36% selected October; the median estimate for the peak policy rate rose to 1.75% from 1.5%.

Japanese sovereign auctions showed demand across both the front end and off-the-run maturities. The three-month Treasury Discount Bill sale produced a 0.9107% weighted-average yield, down from 0.9294% at the June 12 auction. The yield at the lowest accepted price was 0.9224%, compared with 0.9387% previously. Competitive bids totaled JPY9.638 trillion, of which JPY3.150 trillion was accepted for securities maturing September 24.

A liquidity-enhancement auction covering JGBs with five to eleven years remaining accepted JPY648.9 billion from JPY1.898 trillion of bids. The average accepted spread was 0.016 percentage point above the reference rate and the highest accepted spread was 0.020 percentage point. Both Japanese operations settle June 22.

India’s bond market faced a different liquidity problem. Five-year government yields had declined by more than 30 basis points to 6.49% after a June 5 tax reduction encouraged foreign investment in debt. Analysts at Bank of America and Bandhan AMC warned that the short-end rally could lose momentum if the Reserve Bank of India withdraws excess banking cash.

Surplus liquidity, only about 294 billion rupees after recent tax payments, could rise toward 8 trillion rupees as government spending and the RBI’s dividend transfer return cash to banks. Reverse-repurchase operations may absorb part of that amount, while DBS expects a possible increase in banks’ cash-reserve requirement in August. Maturing RBI dollar-forward positions would also remove rupee liquidity.

At the same time, at least four Indian lenders are preparing roughly $2.5 billion of dollar-bond sales using an RBI swap facility priced at 1.5% a year. State Bank of India may raise as much as $1 billion, while Axis Bank, Bank of Baroda and Power Finance Corp. are each considering at least $500 million, mainly for five years. The facility lowers the cost of dollar funding while domestic credit growth continues to exceed deposit growth, but the resulting foreign inflows could add to the liquidity that the RBI may subsequently need to drain.

Canada’s April retail report was softer beneath the headline. Nominal sales increased 0.5% to C$73.0 billion, slightly below the 0.6% expectation and slower than March’s 0.9% gain. Sales volumes were unchanged, while the core measure excluding fuel and autos fell 0.7%. Fuel-vendor receipts rose 5.1% and motor-vehicle sales increased 1.7%. Statistics Canada’s preliminary estimate pointed to a 1.0% rise in May, based on responses covering 52.1% of surveyed companies.

Russia’s central bank also lowered its key rate, though by less than economists had expected. Inflation had slowed to 5.3% in May, helped by currency appreciation and higher oil revenue, but officials continued to face fiscal expansion, fuel-price pressure and the risk that logistics costs from the Middle East conflict would reach domestic prices. The smaller-than-anticipated reduction preserved the bank’s cautious approach as investment outside state-linked sectors weakened.

In corporate credit, SpaceX moved ahead with an investment-grade bond sale expected to raise at least $20 billion. The transaction is part of a much larger funding drive for artificial-intelligence infrastructure and space-based data centers. Alphabet, Amazon and other AI-linked borrowers have raised more than $300 billion across credit markets since November, making the SpaceX deal a test of how much additional exposure investors will accept from a capital-intensive theme already dominating issuance.

Federal Reserve governance drew attention after Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman attended a private Bank of America dinner on June 17, hours after the FOMC meeting ended and during the central bank’s communications blackout. Bowman said she did not discuss monetary policy and had complied with all FOMC and ethics rules. The episode came as Chair Kevin Warsh launched a review of how the Fed communicates with investors and the public.

## Next Open-Session Watch

The June 22 reopening will bring several developments into U.S. rates simultaneously: the resumed US-Iran negotiations, the 60-day oil-sale license, the change in UK leadership and the accumulated global inflation data. The key geopolitical uncertainty is whether negotiations restore secure and sustained passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Conflicting statements over nuclear inspections and continued regional fighting leave that outcome unresolved.

China sets its June loan prime rates at 09:00 in Shanghai on June 22. The 1-year rate is 3.00% and the 5-year rate 3.50%, with both expected to remain unchanged. The fixing will indicate whether recent liquidity measures are reaching lending benchmarks without another formal reduction.

Canada releases May consumer prices at 08:30 ET the same day. Headline inflation is expected to rise to 3.0% from 2.8%, with the first release under an updated basket providing a more direct test of energy pass-through than April’s nominal retail-sales gain.

The first U.S. Treasury supply after the holiday consists of $89 billion of 13-week bills and $77 billion of 26-week bills on June 22, both settling June 25. A $65 billion 6-week bill follows June 23. Coupon supply begins with a $69 billion new 2-year note on June 23, followed by a $70 billion new 5-year note on June 24 and a $44 billion new 7-year note on June 25, all settling June 30. The sequence will test policy-sensitive and intermediate-duration demand after the Fed’s more inflation-focused June message.

Japan’s next sovereign-demand test is an approximately JPY2.5 trillion 5-year JGB auction on June 23. An approximately JPY700 billion reopening of the 20-year JGB due March 2046 follows June 25. The results will help distinguish demand for intermediate maturities from the term-premium pressure affecting longer debt as the BOJ tightens and its board composition evolves.

The principal U.S. macro cluster arrives June 25 at 08:30 ET. May personal income is expected to rise 0.4%, spending 0.6%, headline PCE prices 0.5% and core PCE prices 0.3% on the month. Forecasters expect annual PCE inflation to accelerate to 4.1% from 3.8% in April. Durable-goods orders are expected to fall 5.0% after a 7.9% increase, while the third estimate of Q1 GDP is expected at 1.7% annualized, compared with the prior 1.6% estimate. Initial claims, previously 226,000, will show whether the recent increase in continuing claims is developing into broader labor-market weakness.

Banco de Mexico decides later June 25. The overnight target is 6.50%, and the expected outcome is no change. Energy inflation and the risk of further dollar strength will determine whether policymakers continue to treat the easing cycle as closed.

section_summaries.summary: With U.S. fixed-income markets fully closed for Juneteenth and no Treasury price discovery, the June 22 reopening must absorb a 5 bp rise in the 10-year gilt yield to 4.81% after Andy Burnham’s election victory, firmer European price signals, a more hawkish BOJ debate and still-conditional oil risks around resumed US-Iran talks.

section_summaries.market_read: Longer UK fiscal horizons could create near-term investment room but ask investors to accept a slower debt-stabilization path.
section_summaries.section_title: Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments
section_summaries.summary: UK fiscal credibility became the central sovereign concern as Burnham’s advisers pressed for longer debt-rule horizons and more investment room, while resilient May retail sales complicated the gilt outlook. The ECB defended its increase to 2.25% as German producer inflation accelerated, and BOJ Deputy Governor Himino warned that faster cost pass-through could lift underlying inflation above 2%. India weighed a liquidity-driven short-end rally against possible RBI drains, while SpaceX prepared an investment-grade sale of at least $20 billion amid heavy AI-linked issuance.

The June 22 reopening concentrates geopolitical, policy and supply tests: Hormuz security and the durability of US-Iran talks, China’s 09:00 Shanghai loan prime-rate fixing, Canada’s 08:30 ET CPI release and U.S. bill supply. From June 23–25, new 2-, 5- and 7-year Treasury notes meet the market, Japan sells 5- and 20-year JGBs, and the June 25 U.S. PCE, durable-goods, GDP and claims cluster tests the Fed’s inflation-focused message.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
U.S. fixed-income markets were fully closed for Juneteenth, so there was no same-day Treasury price discovery. In open European markets, the 10-year gilt yield rose 5 basis points to 4.81% after Andy Burnham’s decisive parliamentary victory opened a route to replace Prime Minister Keir Starmer. The selloff reflected concern that advisers favoring longer fiscal horizons and more borrowing for investment could weaken the framework supporting confidence in UK debt, even though Burnham has pledged to keep the existing rules.

European inflation signals also firmed. ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane defended the deposit-rate increase to 2.25% and expects inflation to remain above 3% for the rest of 2026, while German producer prices accelerated to 2.2% annually in May. In Japan, BOJ Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino warned that faster business-cost pass-through could lift underlying inflation above the 2% target, reinforcing the case for further tightening after the policy rate reached 1%.

US-Iran negotiations resumed in Switzerland after an earlier postponement, and Washington issued a 60-day license permitting Iranian oil sales while talks continue. That step offered a path toward greater supply, but disagreement over nuclear inspections, continued regional fighting and uncertainty over secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz left the inflation consequences unresolved ahead of the June 22 U.S. reopening.
